[[Category:Function space]]
A '''function space''' is a [[vector space]] of [[function]]s.

== Formal definition ==

=== The ambient space $\mathbb{F}^X$ ===

Let $X\ne \emptyset$ be a [[set]] and $\mathbb{F}$ a [[field (mathematical concept)|field]].

Let

$$
\mathbb{F}^X \;=\; \{\, f : X \to \mathbb{F} \,\}
$$

be the set of '''all''' functions from $X$ to $\mathbb{F}$,

define addition and scalar multiplication:

$$
\forall f,g \in \mathbb{F}^X,\, c \in \mathbb{F},\, x \in X: \\
(f+g)(x) := f(x)+g(x),\,
(c\cdot f)(x) := c\,f(x),
$$

then $(\mathbb{F}^X,+,\cdot)$ is the '''ambient space''' over $\mathbb{F}$.

<blockquote>
The zero vector is the zero function $0(x)=0$.
</blockquote>

=== Definition of a function space ===

If $V \subseteq \mathbb{F}^X$

satisfies that:

# $\mathbf{0}(x) \in V$ (existence of zero-vector);
# $\forall f,g\in V: f+g \in V$;
# $\forall f\in V,\, c\in\mathbb{F}: cf\in V$.

then $(V,+,\cdot)$ is a '''function space''' over $\mathbb{F}$.
